clue.text: Mr Reagan in the seat of authority

indicators.note: in tells us the Reagan name goes inside the word that follows it

parts.note: Ronald Reagan, US president, known as Ron

explanation.surface: Ronald Reagan sitting in the seat of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ceremonial chair is the emblem and seat of royal power.

clue.text: Kick up a fuss about a Mediterranean island?

indicators.note: about means the island goes around the single letter given by the clue

parts.note: Crete is the large Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Someone making a scene over a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the island CRETE round A. To 'create' is British slang for making a noisy fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British use, to create means to complain loudly or make a scene.

clue.text: Leathery joints from the butcher's?

parts.note: the joints are cuts of meat from a sheep's back, and 'leathery' points to the leather seats a rider uses

explanation.walkthrough: A saddle is both a leather seat for a horse rider and a butcher's cut from the back of a sheep or lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: The butcher's cut from a sheep's loin shares its name with a leather riding seat.

clue.text: Lower in status

parts.note: a plain description: to reduce someone's rank, a grade being a step on a scale

explanation.definitionFit: To demote or debase someone is to drop them a grade.

clue.text: Leave the clubhouse to enter a top-grade golfing event?

definitions.meaning: to step out from indoors into the open air
the Open is golf's British championship, so to take part is to join it

explanation.surface: A golfer leaving the clubhouse to play in a major championship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is the British Open Championship, one of golf's four major tournaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerge into public view, or literally sign up to the Open Championship in golf.

clue.text: A hedge-sparrow otherwise under stress

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the second word sits below the first one

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or you'll be late'

explanation.surface: A small bird that is stressed out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' places OR beneath ACCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunnock, or hedge-sparrow, belongs to the bird family Prunellidae, also called accentors.

clue.text: Sad peers cunningly calumniated

indicators.note: cunningly suggests the letters of the two words are slyly rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: To asperse someone is to slander or defame their character.

clue.text: Lack of resourcefulness? That was Micawber's trouble

definitions.meaning: read as having no resources, that is, no money
Mr Micawber in Dickens's David Copperfield was always in debt

explanation.walkthrough: 'Resourcefulness' is read as being full of resources (funds), not as ingenuity.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without funds is a lack of resources; Dickens's Micawber was perpetually broke.

clue.text: See 8
Sticky sweet?

definitions.meaning: glue or tree resin that sticks things together
a chewy confection such as a wine ...

explanation.definitionFit: Glue is a gummy substance, and a chewy jelly confection is also called by the same name.

clue.text: An outwardly not so hot kitchen utensil

indicators.note: outwardly says the comparative word wraps round the opening word of the clue

parts.note: less hot is colder

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool that is a little cooler on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A perforated bowl for draining vegetables is a kitchen utensil.

clue.text: One by one, they step on to the field

definitions.text: One by one, they step on to the field

parts.words: One by one, they step on to the field
parts.note: a cricket or football side walks out onto the pitch, each player a single unit of the team

explanation.walkthrough: A cricket or football team has this many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team takes the field with this many players.

clue.text: A job that will always keep one busy

definitions.text: A job that will always keep one busy

parts.words: A job that will always keep one busy
parts.note: a chore that can never be finished

explanation.definitionFit: A chore without end will occupy someone forever.

clue.text: Initially a big shot for sixpence, apparently

definitions.meaning: the initials of very important person, a big shot
VI is six in Roman numerals and P is pence

explanation.walkthrough: Sixpence was an old British coin; written VI P it looks like the initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials stand for very important person, a celebrity or bigwig.

clue.text: Wording put below a picture of Pontiac, maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the name could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Text under a photo of the Native American chief Pontiac.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontiac was an 18th-century Ottawa chief, and also a car brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of text printed beneath an illustration describes it.

clue.text: Charming Arab about to swindle the French?

indicators.note: about means the Arab word wraps round the cheating verb

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A charming Arab on the point of conning the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swindle' reads as the Arab's purpose in the surface, but it is a piece of wordplay; 'do' is informal British for cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delightful or lovable is charming.

clue.text: Where the minister used to get his bacon from years ago?

definitions.text: Where the minister used to get his bacon from years ago?

parts.words: Where the minister used to get his bacon from years ago?
parts.note: the parish clergyman was once owed a tenth of farm produce, including one piglet in ten

explanation.walkthrough: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid to the Church; a parson might receive a pig as his share.
explanation.definitionFit: The piglet handed to the parson as a tenth share of a litter.

clue.text: Rhode Island line about a session of bullfighting

indicators.note: about tells us the string wraps round the US state abbreviation

parts.note: a cord is a thin line or string
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A line about a state, then a bullfight.
explanation.walkthrough: A corrida de toros is the Spanish name for a bullfight; the clue's 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish bullfight event is called by its Spanish word for a run or course.

clue.text: A speech designed to further international understanding

definitions.text: A speech designed to further international understanding

parts.words: A speech designed to further international understanding
parts.note: speech here means a language, one constructed for use between nations

explanation.walkthrough: Ido is an invented language derived from Esperanto.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial language based on Esperanto, created to help nations communicate.

clue.text: Produces results

definitions.meaning: to effect something is to bring it about

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means brings about; as a noun, consequences.

clue.text: Most unpopular with the electorate

parts.note: a candidate ranked last in a vote or survey of voters

explanation.definitionFit: Finishing last in a vote or opinion survey shows the least support.

clue.text: A word of more than one meaning

definitions.text: A word of more than one meaning

parts.words: A word of more than one meaning
parts.note: read as a word that means more than one, not a word with several senses

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an ambiguous word; really it is a word whose meaning is 'more than one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical term for a form denoting more than one.

clue.text: Adventurous US writer regarded here as capital

definitions.meaning: Jack ..., author of The Call of the Wild
the capital of the UK, as seen from Britain

explanation.walkthrough: Jack London wrote adventure stories of the Klondike; 'here' means Britain, where the paper was printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London the American novelist, and Britain's capital city.

clue.text: A warning that's hollow at the finish

indicators.note: the finish says the small word goes at the end of the other one

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock

explanation.surface: A warning that the ending is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the finish' reads as part of the definition's sentence but tells you where the small word goes; caveat is Latin for 'let him beware'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin-derived term for a caution or proviso.

clue.text: A particularly persuasive language master?

parts.note: someone with a gift for words who can sway an audience

explanation.definitionFit: A fluent, expressive speaker has mastery of language and persuades well.

clue.text: The trouble the emperor Claudius had to face

definitions.text: The trouble the emperor Claudius had to face

parts.words: The trouble the emperor Claudius had to face
parts.note: Claudius was said to twitch; a facial twitch is a trouble 'to face'

explanation.walkthrough: 'to face' reads as confronting a problem, but means a twitch on the face; Claudius had nervous twitches.
explanation.definitionFit: An involuntary twitch of the facial muscles.

clue.text: A pound to one no colourless personality

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Betting odds of a pound to one on a dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lacking pigment in skin and hair is without colour.

clue.text: Bewildered democrat located in Gwynedd under old spell

definitions.text: located in Gwynedd under old spell

indicators.note: bewildered suggests the letters of the political word are confused and reordered

explanation.surface: A confused democrat, under an old enchantment, in North Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old spell' reads as an enchantment, but means old spelling: Tremadoc is the former spelling of Tremadog, a town in Gwynedd, Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The former spelling of the Welsh town Tremadog, in Gwynedd county.
